# Template Models

This tutorial introduces to custom models with the package `housepi`.
To create a custom model, we recommend not starting from scratch, but instead to copy a template model and modify all its relevant parts.

To copy a template to a custom path we use the function `template_household_model`:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# copy the heterogeneous chain binomial template to a custom directory
my_model_path <- "custom_folder"
housepi::template_household_model(which = "chain-binomial-heterogeneous",
                                  path = my_model_path)
```

Modify all relevant parts of the C++ implementation *model.cpp* and of the header *model.h* within your model directory (see guidelines below).

We can then generate an instance of our custom model from its path. All other methods remain the same already seen in [Walkthrough](walkthrough.html).

```{r, eval=FALSE}
hhmodel <- housepi::HouseholdModel$new(my_model_path)
```

By default a new instance requires the model compilation which is repeated at every R session. 
In certain conditions, e. g. when running different scripts in parallel, we might want to avoid this.
Consider storing the associated model environment as if it was a template with the option `as_template= TRUE`. 

## Hints of the Coding Framework

Assuming that the user knows about basic usage of C++, we provide here a brief introduction on how to use the most relevant classes in `housepi`.

* `Household` class. 
It collects all methods to acces properties of its residents (i. e. individuals sharing the same "house_id" in the data). 
*Getter Methods*
- `data`: value of data entry associated to resident `i`.
- `augm`: value of augmented variable associated to resident `i`.
- `infectious_set`: set of resident indexes with infectious status. 
- `missing_status_set`: set of resident indexes with missing status.
- `susceptible_set`: set of indexes of other residents.
  
* `Model` class. 
It collects all the model specific methods used by its parent class `MCMC` which privately performs the actual computations.
*Getter Methods*
- `param`: value of parameter.
- `param_pointer`: pointer to a parameter.
- `uniform`: uniform random variable.

## Final Comments with Best Practices

* To avoid errors we recommend changing only the chunks of code indicated with "CHANGE-ME".

* Do not introduce constant variables as digits, but rather associate a a constant parameter to them.
E. g. imagine we want to implement a transmission rate in household of size $n$ of the kind 
$\beta \dfrac{4}{n}$,
where $\beta$ is the transmission rate for the reference household size. We can implement it like

```{Rcpp, eval=FALSE}
// ...within a Model method containing (a reference to) a Household object 'house'
transmission_rate = param("beta") * param("ref_size") / house.size();
```

* This will improve readibility, it will allow changes without recompilation, plus it will avoid type-related errors which are frequent in C++ implementation (e.g. is (1/2==0) ? yes!). 

* Core C++ code and template model use "snake case" code syntax. You can find [here](https://style.tidyverse.org/syntax.html) some motivation on why you should too.

### Common mistakes moving from R to C++

* In C++, to access the first element of a vector of size N we use the index 0. The last element can be access with index N-1.

* Don't forget semicolons `;` at the end of your code lines.
